title: 1992 AHSME Problem 11
statement: The ratio of the radii of two concentric circles is \(1:3.\) If \(\overline{AC}\) is a diameter of the larger circle, \(\overline{BC}\) is a chord of the larger circle that is tangent to the smaller circle, and \(AB=12,\) then the radius of the larger circle is

solutions.text:
Let \(O\) be the common center and \(T\) the tangency point on \(\overline{BC}.\) Since \(OT\perp BC\) and \(\angle ABC=90^\circ,\) triangles \(OTC\) and \(ABC\) are similar. If the larger radius is \(R,\) then \(OT=\frac{R}{3},\) \(OC=R,\) and \(AC=2R.\) Thus \[ \frac{OT}{AB}=\frac{OC}{AC}=\frac12. \] Hence \(OT=6\) and \(R=3OT=18.\)

Thus the correct answer is B.
hints: Draw the radius to the point where \(\overline{BC}\) touches the smaller circle
